svg.title: Fig. 206 — The Fourier development of the step function: the first four approximations
svg.desc: Redrawn from Robert C. Yates, A Handbook on Curves and Their Properties (1947), Fig. 206, page 232. Section: trigonometric.

g.data-text: The axes, the step function itself (thin lines: y = 0 for −π < x < 0 and y = π for 0 < x < π) and the level y = π/2 through the jump, where all the approximations pass.

The partial sums π/2 + 2 sin x (2), then adding (2/3) sin 3x (3), then (2/5) sin 5x (4): each is an odd wave about the level π/2 that follows the step more and more closely; on each side of the jump they overshoot.
The first approximation (1): the two constant levels π/4 on the left and 3π/4 on the right; and the circles where the curves cross the step levels.
